transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Reyes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marta Alvarez (SummitCare Head of ML), Tomás Ruiz (CTO), Elliot Chang (Data Eng)

Summary:
0:00 - Quick intros and POC goals.
0:05 - Discussed workload sizing (QPS, tokens), multilingual requirements (EN/ES/FR), and domain sensitivity (telehealth).
0:12 - Reviewed open-model shortlist tradeoffs (size, quantization, hallucination risk) and Redwood routing options (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
0:40 - Agreed on 4-week sprint with benchmark plan and success criteria (weighted accuracy/latency/hallucination).

Topics:
- Success criteria: top-level KPIs and weighting, human evaluation plan
- Workload sizing: QPS, concurrency, average/95th token lengths, SLA targets
- Model shortlist: candidate open models and small variant options
- Benchmarks: latency P95, token cost, accuracy/F1 on golden set, hallucination checks
- Timeline: 4-week POC, with a 1-week smoke test, 2-week benchmark run, 1-week ramp and review

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: All rightyy, hey everyone thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, AE on the Redwood team. Priya is our systems SE, she'll lead the bench stuff. Quick round-robin?
[00:12] Marta: Hi, Marta here. Head of ML at SummitCare, I own the evaluation criteria and shepherding reqs.
[00:18] Tomás: Tomás Ruiz, CTO. Mainly concerned about privacy and network topology — VPC or private option.
[00:25] Elliot: Elliot Chang, data eng, I'll handle delivering logs and sample traffic.
[00:30] Priya: Thanks. High-level goal is to replace current rule-based triage and intent extraction with an LLM-powered service that can handle 6 languages, reduce fallback rate by 60%, and keep P95 latency under 400ms for 95% of requests.
[00:45] Marta: Yup, main success criteria are accuracy on clinical routing, low hallucination for patient instructions, and regulatory auditability. We also care about cost — but accuracy and safety are higher priority.
[01:05] Jordan: Great — can you give us rough volume? QPS, token sizes?
[01:12] Elliot: Current peak is about 35 QPS for the routing endpoint, average request 65 tokens, 95th around 260 tokens, with spikes up to 400 tokens during long transcripts. Monthly active unique sessions ~1.2M.
[01:30] Priya: Helpful. For bench planning we'll simulate 40 QPS sustained with a concurrency mix to hit those tail tokens. We'll also include multi-turn prefixes since you mentioned transcripts.
[01:45] Tomás: On compliance, we need SOC2 + audit logs and KMS integration. Is that available for hosted or only private?
[01:54] Jordan: Hosted supports SOC 2 and KMS for keys at rest, we also offer Dedicated for an isolated GPU pool with stronger controls, and Private for VPC/on-prem. We can share the SOC2 cert and security pack after.
[02:10] Marta: For multilingual — English and Spanish are critical, French and German are medium, Japanese is low-priority but would be nice. We need language parity checks.
[02:22] Priya: We'll run language-specific test suites during the bench. Our harness supports per-locale metrics and per-intent confusion matrices.
[02:30] Jordan: Ok let's talk model shortlist. From our prior intake, we propose three primary candidates and a smaller fast variant for latency-sensitive routes:
[02:40] - Mistral-Instruct-7B (open-instruct style) — good accuracy for instruction tasks and smaller footprint.
[02:50] - Llama-2-13B (community fine-tuned) — stronger reasoning, but larger cost and higher memory.
[03:00] - RedPajama-Instruct-3B/7B (Mosaic family) — good baseline and predictable quantization.
[03:09] Priya: And a quantized 4-bit variant of the 7B models for throughput comparisons; also a distilled 3B we can try for routing-only fast path.
[03:18] Marta: Hmm. Any concerns about hallucination with the 7Bs? Clinical content is sensitive.
[03:24] Priya: Great question. Smaller models tend to hallucinate more on open-ended generation; but for routing and classification with constrained templates and labels, we saw acceptable false positive rates. We'll run a hallucination metric — basically percent of outputs that contradict a gold-response or add clinically risky instructions.
[03:40] Elliot: We'll provide a golden set: 2k annotated examples covering intents + edge cases, and 500 transcripts for multilingual checks. Should we include patient PHI? We will sanitize/replace tokens.
[03:50] Jordan: Perfect. For benchmarking we propose these metrics: P95 latency, tokens/sec throughput, cost-per-1M-tokens, classification accuracy/F1 per intent, hallucination rate, and human eval pass/fail for top 200 high-risk cases.
[04:10] Tomás: What about routing policies? If the model falls back, can Redwood automatically route to a smaller model or to a rule engine to keep SLA?
[04:18] Priya: Yes — smart routing supports fallbacks by policy. You can do model-tier routing: try fast 3B, if confidence low or token budget exceeded, escalate to 7B or route to rules. We can measure confidence threshold during bench to tune the tradeoff latency vs accuracy.
[04:36] Marta: Timeline then? We're aiming for a vendor decision mid-April. Is a 4-week POC realistic?
[04:44] Jordan: Yes — recommended sprint: 1 week infra + smoke test, 2 weeks full bench runs across models and locales, 1 week for analysis, human eval, and review. That fits a decision by mid-April if we start the week of March 30.
[04:58] Priya: We'll provide a benchmark plan doc that maps tests to days so you can follow progress.
[05:04] Elliot: For infra what access do you need? Service accounts, VPC peering, etc?
[05:10] Priya: For Hosted bench we need API keys and a sandbox dataset; for Dedicated/Private we may need temporary VPC peering details or on-prem happenstance access. We'll send a short infra checklist.
[05:22] Jordan: I'll also include price assumptions: hosted on usage vs dedicated commit tiers — with example math for your 40 QPS and monthly tokens.
[05:30] Marta: On success criteria weights — we plan to weight accuracy 0.5, hallucination 0.3, latency 0.2. We'll send that in writing as an action item.
[05:42] Priya: Good to have weights; that helps the scoring rubric. For hallucination thresholds, do you have a tolerance?
[05:48] Marta: Ideally <1% for high-risk cases, <3% overall. We'll confirm.
[05:55] Jordan: We'll set up the bench to measure that and flag any model above the threshold.
[06:02] Tomás: Any competitors we should benchmark against? We might want a few vendor baselines.
[06:08] Jordan: We can include Anthropic-lite and an OpenAI baseline for black-box comparison — just to show where open models land vs hosted models. There may be API cost for that, we'll include in estimate.
[06:20] Elliot: About logging and audit — we need per-request traces with model version and tokens in/out stored for 90 days. Is that supported?
[06:28] Priya: Yes, Redwood Console supports token-level traces, model tags, and exportable audit logs. For private deployments we can push logs to your S3 or internal bucket.
[06:36] Marta: Anything else we should call out? Edge cases?
[06:40] Priya: We'll do a targeted adversarial set — prompts designed to elicit hallucinations or instruction-following failures. That'll be part of the human eval.
[06:50] Jordan: Okay, recap next steps briefly — action items and timeline.
[06:54] Marta: Sounds good.
[07:00] Jordan: Recap: Jordan sends pricing + Dedicated vs Hosted one-pager by Friday 3/20; Priya uploads bench harness and sample config by Sun 3/22; Elliot shares sanitized samples and token stats by Wed 3/25; Marta to send weighted success criteria by Tue 3/24. Kickoff week of 3/30.
[07:22] Tomás: We'll try to prioritize the sample logs this week.
[07:26] Elliot: I'll get them out tomorrow, thanks.
[07:30] Jordan: Great, we'll also attach an example benchmarking spreadsheet and a link to the security pack.
[07:36] Marta: Thanks, appreciate it.
[07:38] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invite for the kickoff and the links.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mislabels (accented names sometimes mis-typed), filler words present. Links shared in chat: https://drive.google.com/some-bench-plan (shared), security pack: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack (placeholder).

End of transcript.
